title: Draft the value case
description: Record the business outcomes this project is funded to deliver, with the measures that will show whether it did.

title: Outline the solution scope
description: List the processes in scope and, as importantly, the ones deliberately out of it.

title: Baseline the project plan
description: Agree the schedule, milestones and the dates the gates are expected to be reached.

title: Onboard the team and assign roles
description: Name who is accountable for each workstream before the work starts rather than after.

title: Provision the environments
description: Stand up the systems the project needs, and confirm access actually works for the people who need it.

title: Run the fit-to-standard workshops
description: Walk the standard process with the business and classify each requirement as fit, gap or accepted gap.

title: Confirm the backlog
description: Turn the workshop outcomes into a backlog everyone agrees is the work.

title: Agree the data migration scope
description: Decide which objects move, how far back history goes, and who owns the cleansing.

title: Inventory the integrations
description: List every interface, its direction and its owner, including the ones nobody has mentioned yet.

title: Configure and build the solution
description: Deliver the agreed backlog in sprints, keeping configuration decisions traceable to the workshops.

title: Run the test cycles
description: Unit, string, integration and user acceptance, each with an entry and exit condition agreed in advance.

title: Rehearse the data migration
description: A full load against production volumes, timed, so cutover is not the first attempt.

title: Review the extensions
description: Confirm every extension is still needed and built on supported extension points.

title: Approve the cutover plan
description: The hour-by-hour sequence, who does each step, and the point past which rollback stops being an option.

title: Confirm production readiness
description: Performance, security and operational monitoring verified on the system that will actually run.

title: Put the support model in place
description: Who answers the phone in week one, and what they are allowed to change.

title: Confirm the business is ready
description: Training delivered, roles assigned, and the people doing the work know what changes on Monday.

title: Run hypercare
description: Elevated support immediately after go-live, with an agreed threshold for exiting it.

title: Hand over to operations
description: Documentation, runbooks and on-call transferred, and accepted by the team taking them.

title: Establish continuous improvement
description: A standing cycle for release adoption and process improvement. This lives inside Run rather than after it, which is why there is no seventh phase.
